title: Complex rational maps of degree at least two whose periodic multipliers all lie in one number field are power, Chebyshev or Lattes maps
author: Valentin Huguin
difficulty_reason: Equidistribution of Galois orbits applies only after the multiplier-isospectral moduli point has been descended to a number field. The source constructs periodic cycles shadowing a chosen repeller while tracking their periods and characteristic exponents, rather than merely quoting the needed periodic approximation. It then combines those cycles with the arithmetic orbit bounds and exponent rigidity to obtain the exceptional classification, leaving a new dynamical construction beyond the cited equidistribution and rigidity foundations.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Exact MainTheorem, a single fixed number field containing every multiplier at every periodic cycle; rationality over that field of the original map is not assumed. Full1–9read, new repeller approximation6–8 and Galois/exponent proof8–9 included. Theorem6 Autissier equidistribution, McMullen finite multiplier-isospectral fibers outside flexible Lattes locus and Zdunik rigidity are identified prior foundations. Remark8 explicitly describes bounded change to Zdunik proof excluding finitely many low-period points; not an omitted new core. Conclusion permits rigid as well as flexible Lattes and signed power/Chebyshev conjugacy classes. No degree-two, integer-only or imaginary-quadratic parameter variants separately counted. All original context preserved.
